claim: Naive T cell precursor frequency determines the magnitude of immunodominance.
source: Naive T cell precursor frequency determines the magnitude of immunodominance.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an established fact in the field.

claim: A broad T cell repertoire requires diverse positively selecting self-peptides.
source: While a broad T cell repertoire requires diverse positively selecting self-peptides, how a single positively selecting ligand influences naive T cell precursor frequency remains undefined.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: How a single positively selecting ligand influences naive T cell precursor frequency remains undefined.
source: While a broad T cell repertoire requires diverse positively selecting self-peptides, how a single positively selecting ligand influences naive T cell precursor frequency remains undefined.
evidence: This is stated as a knowledge gap in the abstract.

claim: The authors generated a transgenic mouse expressing gp250 as the only MHC class II I-Ek ligand.
source: We generated a transgenic mouse expressing a naturally occurring self-peptide, gp250, that positively selects an MCC-specific TCR, AND, as the only MHC class II I-Ek ligand to study the MCC highly organized immunodominance hierarchy.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental approach in the abstract.

claim: gp250 positively selects the MCC-specific TCR AND.
source: We generated a transgenic mouse expressing a naturally occurring self-peptide, gp250, that positively selects an MCC-specific TCR, AND, as the only MHC class II I-Ek ligand to study the MCC highly organized immunodominance hierarchy.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by previous work cited in the manuscript (Lo et al., 2009).

claim: The single gp250/I-Ek ligand greatly enhanced MCC-tetramer+ CD4+ T cells.
source: The single gp250/I-Ek ligand greatly enhanced MCC-tetramer+ CD4+ T cells, and skewed MCC-tetramer+ population toward V11α+Vβ3+, a major TCR pair in MCC-specific immunodominance.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 3.

claim: The gp250/I-Ek ligand skewed the MCC-tetramer+ population toward Vα11+Vβ3+.
source: The single gp250/I-Ek ligand greatly enhanced MCC-tetramer+ CD4+ T cells, and skewed MCC-tetramer+ population toward V11α+Vβ3+, a major TCR pair in MCC-specific immunodominance.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: Vα11+Vβ3+ is a major TCR pair in MCC-specific immunodominance.
source: The single gp250/I-Ek ligand greatly enhanced MCC-tetramer+ CD4+ T cells, and skewed MCC-tetramer+ population toward V11α+Vβ3+, a major TCR pair in MCC-specific immunodominance.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract and supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: The gp250-selected Vα11+Vβ3+ CD4+ T cells had a significantly increased frequency of conserved MCC-preferred CDR3 features.
source: The gp250-selected V11α+Vβ3+ CD4+ T cells had a significantly increased frequency of conserved MCC-preferred CDR3 features.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 6.

claim: There is a direct and causal relationship between a selecting self-peptide and the specificity of the selected TCRs.
source: Our studies establish a direct and causal relationship between a selecting self-peptide and the specificity of the selected TCRs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the study.

claim: An immunodominant T cell response can be due to a dominant positively selecting self-peptide.
source: Thus, an immunodominant T cell response can be due to a dominant positively selecting self-peptide.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, inferred from the experimental data.

claim: During an infection, generally only a fraction of epitopes actually stimulate T cell response.
source: An individual pathogen encodes thousands of potentially immunogenic epitopes, yet during the course of an infection, generally only a fraction of epitopes actually stimulate T cell response (Sercarz et al., 1993; Sant et al., 2007; Weaver and Sant, 2009; Jenkins et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: Immunodominance is a fundamental feature of T cell responses.
source: This fundamental feature of T cell responses is known as immunodominance (Sercarz et al., 1993; Chen et al., 2001; Yewdell and Del Val, 2004; Yewdell, 2006; Sant et al., 2007; Weaver and Sant, 2009; Jenkins and Moon, 2012).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: Most immunodominance studies have focused on the antigen presentation and processing pathways.
source: Most of the effort in immunodominance studies has focused on the antigen presentation and processing pathways (Deng et al., 1993; van Ham et al., 1996; Nanda and Sant, 2000; Chen et al., 2001; Crowe et al., 2003; Chen and McCluskey, 2006; Lazarski et al., 2006; Yewdell, 2006; Weaver and Sant, 2009).
evidence: This is stated as a summary of the field supported by multiple citations.

claim: Immunodominance is also defined by the frequencies of naive T cells specific for individual antigens.
source: Yet immunodominance is also defined by the frequencies of naive T cells specific for individual antigens (Kotturi et al., 2008; Jenkins and Moon, 2012; Kwok et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Thymic positive selection serves as a major developmental process to generate mature T cell repertoires.
source: Given that thymic positive selection serves as a major developmental process to generate mature T cell repertoires (Jameson et al., 1995; Morris and Allen, 2012), one may reason positive selection would play a role in determining naive T cell precursor frequency to dictate immunodominance.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The frequency of T cells specific for individual peptide–MHC ligands is at most about 20–100 cells per million naive T cells.
source: First, the frequency of T cells specific for individual peptide–MHC ligands is at most about 20–100 cells per million naive T cells (Jenkins and Moon, 2012), making it difficult to identify such an infrequent population.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: The murine CD4+ T cell response against cytochrome c is an outstanding model system to investigate the impact of positively selecting ligands on immunodominance.
source: The murine CD4+ T cell response against cytochrome c is an outstanding model system to investigate the impact of positively selecting ligands on immunodominance (Solinger et al., 1979; Schwartz, 1985; Engel and Hedrick, 1988).
evidence: This is stated as a rationale for the model system used, supported by citations.

claim: Only one single dominant epitope emerges from the immunization of H−2k mice with the whole protein of moth cytochrome c (MCC) or closely related pigeon cytochrome c (PCC).
source: Only one single dominant epitope emerges from the immunization of H−2k mice with the whole protein of moth cytochrome c (MCC) or closely related pigeon cytochrome c (PCC) (Hedrick et al., 1982; Winoto et al., 1986; Hedrick et al., 1988; McHeyzer-Williams and Davis, 1995).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about the MCC model system, supported by citations.

claim: The MCC- or PCC-stimulated CD4+ T cell response shows highly organized immunodominance hierarchies.
source: Also, the MCC- or PCC-stimulated CD4+ T cell response shows highly organized immunodominance hierarches.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about the MCC model system.

claim: The MCC- or PCC-specific responses are highly dominated by Vα11+ TCR.
source: The MCC- or PCC-specific responses are highly dominated by Vα11+ TCR, and exhibit several conserved CDR3 features (Winoto et al., 1986; Hedrick et al., 1988; McHeyzer-Williams and Davis, 1995; McHeyzer-Williams et al., 1999; Mikszta et al., 1999; Newell et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: MCC-specific responses exhibit several conserved CDR3 features.
source: The MCC- or PCC-specific responses are highly dominated by Vα11+ TCR, and exhibit several conserved CDR3 features (Winoto et al., 1986; Hedrick et al., 1988; McHeyzer-Williams and Davis, 1995; McHeyzer-Williams et al., 1999; Mikszta et al., 1999; Newell et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: During MCC-specific responses, the Vα11+Vβ3+ CD4+ T cells are the most dominant responders.
source: During MCC-specific responses, the Vα11+Vβ3+ CD4+ T cells are the most dominant responders, while Vα11+ TCRs pairing with Vβ6+, Vβ8+, or Vβ14+ are the subdominant responders (Miyazaki et al., 1996; Malherbe et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Vα11+ TCRs pairing with Vβ6+, Vβ8+, or Vβ14+ are subdominant responders during MCC-specific responses.
source: During MCC-specific responses, the Vα11+Vβ3+ CD4+ T cells are the most dominant responders, while Vα11+ TCRs pairing with Vβ6+, Vβ8+, or Vβ14+ are the subdominant responders (Miyazaki et al., 1996; Malherbe et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Certain positions at CDR3α and CDR3β regions present highly conserved amino acid usages where TCR makes contact with MCC peptide.
source: Based on the structural data, certain positions at CDR3α and CDR3β regions, where TCR make contact with MCC peptide, present highly conserved amino acid usages (McHeyzer-Williams et al., 1999; Newell et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge based on structural data, supported by citations.

claim: MCC/I-Ek tetramers can detect most primary MCC-specific T cells.
source: Moreover, the MCC/I-Ek tetramers have been shown to be able to detect most primary MCC-specific T cells (Savage et al., 1999).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: The laboratory had previously identified gp250 as a naturally occurring positively selecting self-peptide for the AND TCR.
source: Importantly, our laboratory had previously identified a naturally occurring positively selecting self-peptide, termed gp250, for its ability to positively select the MCC-specific TCR: AND (Lo et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated as previous work from the authors' laboratory, supported by a citation.

claim: The covalently linked gp250/I-Ekβ successfully paired with transgenic I-Ekα in gp250 SC mice.
source: In gp250 SC mice, the transgenic covalently linked gp250/I-Ekβ successfully paired with transgenic I-Ekα, restoring the surface expression of I-Ek in splenic B cells and CD11c+ dendritic cells (Figure 1A–D).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the experiments, supported by data in Figure 1.

claim: The gp250/I-Ek expression restored surface expression of I-Ek in splenic B cells and CD11c+ dendritic cells.
source: In gp250 SC mice, the transgenic covalently linked gp250/I-Ekβ successfully paired with transgenic I-Ekα, restoring the surface expression of I-Ek in splenic B cells and CD11c+ dendritic cells (Figure 1A–D).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the experiments, supported by data in Figure 1.

claim: The level of gp250/I-Ek expression was approximately 10% on B cells and 40% on dendritic cells compared to wild-type.
source: The level of expression of the gp250/I-Ek was readily detectable, but reconstituted to approximately a 10% level on B cells and 40% on dendritic cells (Figure 1A–D).
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from the experiments, supported by data in Figure 1.

claim: Immunofluorescence staining showed surface expression of I-Ek in the cortex and medulla of the thymus in gp250 SC mice.
source: Immunofluorescence staining of thymic frozen sections of gp250 SC mice showed surface expression of I-Ek in the cortex and medulla of the thymus (data not shown).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from immunofluorescence experiments.

claim: The covalently linked gp250/I-Ek positively selected a large number of CD4+ T cells in the thymus with an average of 1.6 × 10^8 total thymocytes and 6.8 × 10^7 CD4SP T cells.
source: The covalently linked gp250/I-Ek positively selected a large number of CD4+ T cells in the thymus with an average of 1.6 × 108 total thymocytes and 6.8 × 107 CD4SP T cells (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from the experiments, supported by data in Figure 2.

claim: The positive selection efficiency for CD4SP T cells in the gp250 SC mouse was approximately 40% of that seen in the B6.K wild type.
source: The positive selection efficiency for CD4SP T cells in the gp250 SC mouse was approximately 40% of that seen in the B6.K wild type (Figure 2B,C), in line with other published single chain mice.
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison from the experiments, supported by data in Figure 2.

claim: The size of CD8SP T cells in gp250 SC mouse was comparable to that in B6.K.
source: The size of CD8SP T cells in gp250 SC mouse was comparable to that in B6.K (Figure 2D), as anticipated given that the gp250 SC mice expressed normal class I molecules.
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison from the experiments, supported by data in Figure 2.

claim: The peripheral CD4+ T cell population in gp250 SC mice was around 40% of the B6.K, yet still averaged 1.7 × 10^6 CD4+ T cells per spleen.
source: In the spleen, the peripheral CD4+ T cell population in gp250 SC mice was readily detectable, being around 40% of the B6.K, yet still averaged 1.7 × 106 CD4+ T cells per spleen (Figure 2E–G).
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from the experiments, supported by data in Figure 2.

claim: The single gp250/I-Ek ligand selected a full TCR Vβ repertoire without complete absence of any Vβs.
source: The single gp250/I-Ek ligand selected a full TCR Vβ repertoire, in that we did not observe any complete absence of Vβs (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an observation from the experiments, supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The frequencies of some TCR Vβs were decreased in gp250 SC mice, including Vβ2+, Vβ4+, Vβ8.1/8.2+.
source: However, the frequencies of some TCR Vβs were decreased, including Vβ2+, Vβ4+, Vβ8.1/8.2+, suggesting gp250/I-Ek did not positively select individual Vβs with a uniform selection capability (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is an observation from the experiments, supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The usages of Vβ5+, Vβ11+, and Vβ12+ were increased in peripheral CD4+ T cells in gp250 SC mice.
source: The usages of Vβ5+, Vβ11+, and Vβ12+ were also increased in peripheral CD4+ T cells in gp250 SC mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is an observation from the experiments, supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: In B6.K > gp250 chimeras, the frequencies of Vβ5+, Vβ11+ and Vβ12+ were indistinguishable when compared with B6.K > B6.K chimeras.
source: After a 12-week reconstitution, in B6.K > gp250 chimeras, the frequencies of Vβ5+, Vβ11+ and Vβ12+ were indistinguishable when compared with B6.K > B6.K chimeras (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: This is an observation from bone marrow chimera experiments, supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C,D.

claim: The increased Vβs in gp250 SC mice were caused by the lack of negative selection.
source: Given gp250/I-Ek was the only ligand presented by MHC class II molecules in gp250 SC mice, it was possible that the increased Vβs were caused by the lack of negative selection. We therefore used B6.K hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) to reconstitute lethally irradiated gp250 SC mice (B6.K > gp250 SC; Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental design and results of the bone marrow chimera experiments.

claim: The gp250-mediated positive selection dramatically expanded the MCC-specific CD4+ T cell response, showing a threefold increase in the periphery and a twofold increase in the thymus compared with B6.K mice.
source: The gp250-mediated positive selection dramatically expanded the MCC-specific CD4+ T cell response (Figure 3). In gp250 SC mice, the MCC tetramer+ CD4+ population showed a threefold increase in the periphery and a twofold increase in the thymus, compared with the population in B6.K mice (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from the experiments, supported by data in Figure 3.

claim: The MCC tetramer+ population was uniquely expanded in the gp250-selected CD4+ T cell repertoire.
source: Indeed, the MCC tetramer+ population was uniquely expanded in the gp250-selected CD4+ T cell repertoire, as the frequency of the hemoglobin antigen (Hb) tetramer-bound CD4+ T cell population was equivalent, if not slightly decreased (Figure 3C,D).
evidence: This is an observation from the experiments comparing MCC and Hb tetramer staining, supported by data in Figure 3.

claim: The frequency of Hb tetramer-bound CD4+ T cell population was equivalent or slightly decreased in gp250 SC mice compared to B6.K.
source: Indeed, the MCC tetramer+ population was uniquely expanded in the gp250-selected CD4+ T cell repertoire, as the frequency of the hemoglobin antigen (Hb) tetramer-bound CD4+ T cell population was equivalent, if not slightly decreased (Figure 3C,D).
evidence: This is an observation from the experiments, supported by data in Figure 3C,D.

claim: After 12-week reconstitution, the frequency of MCC tetramer+ CD4+ T cells was 1.5% in B6.K HSC-reconstituted gp250 SC mice.
source: After a 12-week reconstitution, the frequency of MCC tetramer+ CD4+ T cells was 1.5% in B6.K HSC-reconstituted gp250 SC mice (Figure 3E,F).
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from bone marrow chimera experiments, supported by data in Figure 3E,F.

claim: gp250-mediated positive selection enriched MCC tetramer+ cells more than eightfold compared to B6.K HSC-reconstituted B6.K mice.
source: Compared with the frequency of MCC tetramer+ population in B6.K HSC-reconstituted B6.K mice, which was about 0.18%, gp250-mediated positive selection enriched MCC tetramer+ cells more than eightfold (Figure 3E,F).
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison from bone marrow chimera experiments, supported by data in Figure 3E,F.

claim: The augmented MCC tetramer+ population in gp250 SC mice was not due to the lack of negative selection.
source: The B6.K HSC-reconstituted gp250 chimeras suggested the augmented MCC tetramer+ population in gp250 SC mice was not due to the lack of negative selection.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the bone marrow chimera experiments.

claim: In B6.K CD4+ T cells, the MCC tetramer+ populations that used Vα11− vs Vα11+ were about equal.
source: In B6.K CD4+ T cells, the MCC tetramer+ populations that used Vα11− vs Vα11+ were about equal, whereas in gp250 SC mice, the vast majority of MCC tetramer+ population expressed Vα11+ (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This is an observation from the experiments, supported by data in Figure 4A,B.

claim: In gp250 SC mice, the vast majority of MCC tetramer+ population expressed Vα11+.
source: In B6.K CD4+ T cells, the MCC tetramer+ populations that used Vα11− vs Vα11+ were about equal, whereas in gp250 SC mice, the vast majority of MCC tetramer+ population expressed Vα11+ (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This is an observation from the experiments, supported by data in Figure 4A,B.

claim: The frequency of Vα11− MCC tetramer+ population in gp250 SC mice was comparable with the frequency in B6.K mice.
source: It was the increased Vα11+ MCC tetramer+ cells that specifically contributed to the enlarged MCC tetramer+ population in gp250 SC mice, since the frequency of Vα11− MCC tetramer+ population in gp250 SC mice was comparable with the frequency in B6.K mice (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is an observation from the experiments, supported by data in Figure 4B.

claim: gp250/I-Ek specifically favored the positive selection of Vα11+ TCR.
source: The exclusively enlarged Vα11+ MCC tetramer+ population in gp250 SC mice suggested that gp250/I-Ek specifically favored the positive selection of Vα11+ TCR, thus resulting in a T cell repertoire profile with the enhanced MCC tetramer-bound population.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the experimental observations.

claim: The sorted MCC tetramer+ CD4+ T cells upregulated CD69 when stimulated overnight with MCC-pulsed APC in vitro.
source: The MCC tetramer+ T cells were responsive to MCC, as the sorted MCC tetramer+ CD4+ T cells upregulated CD69 while stimulated overnight with MCC-pulsed APC in vitro (Figure 4C,D).
evidence: This is an observation from in vitro stimulation experiments, supported by data in Figure 4C,D.

claim: The Vα11+-expressing CD4+ T cells significantly increased in the thymus and periphery in gp250 SC mice.
source: The Vα11+-expressing CD4+ T cells significantly increased in the thymus and periphery in gp250 SC mice (Figure 5A,B), suggesting gp250/I-Ek actively skewed the post-selection TCR usages to influence antigen specificities.
evidence: This is an observation from the experiments, supported by data in Figure 5A,B.

claim: gp250/I-Ek actively skewed the post-selection TCR usages to influence antigen specificities.
source: The Vα11+-expressing CD4+ T cells significantly increased in the thymus and periphery in gp250 SC mice (Figure 5A,B), suggesting gp250/I-Ek actively skewed the post-selection TCR usages to influence antigen specificities.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the experimental observations.

claim: MCC-preferred dominant pair Vα11+Vβ3+ increased about 1.4-fold in thymic CD4SP and at least twofold in periphery in gp250 SC mice.
source: While examining the TCR Vβ expression among gp250-selected Vα11+ CD4+ T cells, MCC-preferred dominant pair Vα11+Vβ3+ increased about 1.4-fold in thymic CD4SP and at least twofold in periphery (Figure 5C–E).
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from the experiments, supported by data in Figure 5C–E.

claim: Certain subdominant MCC-preferred TCRs also increased in gp250 SC mice.
source: Certain subdominant MCC-preferred TCRs also increased (Figure 5C–E).
evidence: This is an observation from the experiments, supported by data in Figure 5C–E.

claim: For some Vβs found commonly to pair with Vα11 in normal mice (such as Vβ2 and Vβ4), the frequencies were unchanged in gp250 SC mice.
source: Interestingly, for some Vβs, found commonly to pair with Vα11 in normal mice (such as Vβ2 and Vβ4), the frequencies were unchanged (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is an observation from the experiments, supported by data in Figure 5C.

claim: gp250 specifically promoted the selection of MCC-specific TCR usages.
source: This observation argued that gp250 specifically promoted the selection of MCC-specific TCR usages, and was not merely functioning as a good selecting ligand for all Vα11+.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the experimental observations.

claim: The increased frequency of Vα11+Vβ3+ did not result from the absence of negative selection in gp250 SC mice.
source: The increased frequency of Vα11+Vβ3+ did not result from the absence of negative selection in gp250 SC mice (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is a conclusion from bone marrow chimera experiments, supported by data in Figure 5F.

claim: Vα11+ CD4+ peripheral T cells in B6.K > gp250 SC bone marrow chimeras were about 2.5-fold larger than in B6.K > B6.K chimeras.
source: After a 12-week reconstitution, Vα11+ CD4+ peripheral T cells in B6.K > gp250 SC bone marrow chimeras were about 2.5-fold larger than the size in B6.K > B6.K chimeras (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from bone marrow chimera experiments, supported by data in Figure 5F.

claim: The Vα11+Vβ3+ population increased to approximately threefold in B6.K > gp250 SC chimeras compared with B6.K > B6.K chimera mice.
source: The Vα11+Vβ3+ population increased to approximately threefold in B6.K > gp250 SC chimeras, compared with the population in B6.K > B6.K chimera mice as well (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from bone marrow chimera experiments, supported by data in Figure 5F.

claim: gp250-mediated positive selection was the driving force to cause the enlarged MCC-specific CD4+ population.
source: The bone marrow reconstitution data clearly supported gp250-mediated positive selection was the driving force to cause the enlarged MCC-specific CD4+ population.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the bone marrow chimera experiments.

claim: MCC-responsive CD4+ T cells showed strikingly conserved CDR3 features, including glutamic acid at CDR3 α89, serine at α91, asparagine at CDR3 β97, and alanine/glycine at β99.
source: In addition to the preferred TCR Vα and Vβ usages, MCC-responsive CD4+ T cells also showed strikingly conserved CDR3 features, including the preferred four CDR3 residues: glutamic acid at CDR3 α89 (α89E), serine at α91 (α91S), asparagine at CDR3 β97 (β97N), and alanine/glycine at β99 (β99A/G) (McHeyzer-Williams et al., 1999; Newell et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Crystal structures of TCR:pMHC complexes have provided structural explanation for conserved CDR3 residues forming salt bridges or hydrogen bonds with MCC TCR contact residues at P3 (tyrosine), P5 (lysine), and P8 (threonine).
source: The crystal structures of TCR:pMHC complexes have provided the structural explanation for these conserved CDR3 residues for each may form salt bridge or hydrogen bond with MCC TCR contact residues at P3 (tyrosine), P5 (lysine), and P8 (threonine) (Newell et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge from structural studies, supported by a citation.

claim: The authors successfully recovered 38 sequences of TCR Vα11 from single cell sorted Vα11+Vβ3+ peripheral CD4+ T cells from a gp250 SC mouse.
source: We single cell sorted Vα11+Vβ3+ peripheral CD4+ T cells from a gp250 SC mouse for single cell TCR analysis. We successfully recovered 38 sequences of TCR Vα11 (Table 1), among which five also had the co-expressed Vβ3 sequences identified (Table 2).
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental results.

claim: Five of the 38 Vα11 sequences also had co-expressed Vβ3 sequences identified.
source: We single cell sorted Vα11+Vβ3+ peripheral CD4+ T cells from a gp250 SC mouse for single cell TCR analysis. We successfully recovered 38 sequences of TCR Vα11 (Table 1), among which five also had the co-expressed Vβ3 sequences identified (Table 2).
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental results.

claim: The authors obtained about 2900 unique CDR3α and 1500 CDR3β sequences in gp250-selected Vα11+Vβ3+ CD4+ T cells from bulk sequencing.
source: The Vα11+Vβ3+ populations were also sent for large-scale bulk CDR3α and CDR3β sequencing to extensively explore CDR3 features. We obtained about 2900 unique CDR3α and 1500 CDR3β sequences in gp250-selected Vα11+Vβ3+ CD4+ T cells (Table 3).
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental results.

claim: The authors found AND TCR and its closely related TCRs 5cc7 and 226 in the gp250-selected repertoire.
source: We found AND TCR and its closely related TCR: 5cc7 and 226 TCRs (Tables 1 and 3).
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental results.

claim: In bulk population sequence analysis, the majority of published MCC-reactive TCR CDR3α sequences were identified in the dataset.
source: In bulk population sequence analysis, the majority of published MCC-reactive TCR CDR3α sequences were identified in our dataset, and we found six of the published CDR3β sequences (Table 3) (Hedrick et al., 1988; McHeyzer-Williams et al., 1999).
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental results compared to published data.

claim: Six of the published CDR3β sequences were found in the bulk population sequence analysis.
source: In bulk population sequence analysis, the majority of published MCC-reactive TCR CDR3α sequences were identified in our dataset, and we found six of the published CDR3β sequences (Table 3) (Hedrick et al., 1988; McHeyzer-Williams et al., 1999).
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental results.

claim: gp250-mediated positive selection significantly enriched the usage of serine at CDR3 α91 in Vα11+Vβ3+ CD4+ T cells.
source: Analysis of CDR3α residues in the bulk populations revealed that gp250-mediated positive selection significantly enriched the usage of serine at CDR3 α91 in Vα11+Vβ3+ CD4+ T cells (Figure 6A,B), which hydrogen bonds to the MCC peptide tyrosine residue at P328.
evidence: This is an observation from CDR3 sequencing analysis, supported by data in Figure 6A,B.

claim: Serine at CDR3 α91 hydrogen bonds to the MCC peptide tyrosine residue at P3.
source: Analysis of CDR3α residues in the bulk populations revealed that gp250-mediated positive selection significantly enriched the usage of serine at CDR3 α91 in Vα11+Vβ3+ CD4+ T cells (Figure 6A,B), which hydrogen bonds to the MCC peptide tyrosine residue at P328.
evidence: This is stated as a structural relationship.

claim: In B6.K mice, about 20% of Vα11+Vβ3+ CD4+ T cells expressed serine at CDR3 α91.
source: In B6.K mice, about 20% of Vα11+Vβ3+ CD4+ T cells expressed serine at CDR3 α91, whereas in gp250 SC mice, the frequency was increased 1.5-fold to become about 30% (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from CDR3 sequencing analysis, supported by data in Figure 6A,B.

claim: In gp250 SC mice, about 30% of Vα11+Vβ3+ CD4+ T cells expressed serine at CDR3 α91.
source: In B6.K mice, about 20% of Vα11+Vβ3+ CD4+ T cells expressed serine at CDR3 α91, whereas in gp250 SC mice, the frequency was increased 1.5-fold to become about 30% (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from CDR3 sequencing analysis, supported by data in Figure 6A,B.

claim: A similar 1.5-fold increase of serine at α91 was observed in single cell repertoire analysis compared to published data.
source: We observed a similar 1.5-fold increase of serine at α91 in single cell repertoire analysis compared to the published data (McHeyzer-Williams et al., 1999) (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison from single cell analysis, supported by data in Figure 6B.

claim: gp250-mediated selection had little impact on skewing the amino acid residue at CDR3 α89.
source: However, gp250-mediated selection had little impact on skewing the amino acid residue at CDR3 α89, as α89E usages of Vα11+Vβ3+ CD4+ T cells were comparable with the frequency seen in B6.K (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: This is an observation from CDR3 sequencing analysis, supported by data in Figure 6A,B.

claim: gp250-mediated positive selection dramatically escalated the usages of β97N in Vα11+Vβ3+ CD4+ T cells.
